Data:Mere4.json.label: +++Ereb: Westengryred
Data:Mere4.json.desc: Westengryre is what the early monks of St Brandan's called it; that old green-sickness, the raptness of desolation, the terror of the wastes, and it is upon me now. The Wood. The Wood. The Wood...!

xexts.malady．inflicting: As my spirits sink lower, a creaking fear passes softly into me, like something crawling through a window left carelessly open. [Your Ereb has a Malady.]
xexts.contamination．bloodlines: There are words here which ooze blood - a bloodlines infection. As I wipe the drops carefully away, a fear steals into my soul, like a fear of the dark, but stronger and mustier. [Your Ereb has a Malady; this item is infested.]
xexts.contamination．keeperskin: Luminous splotches of fungus mark this thing. A keeperskin infection. I can see their sickly light even when I close my eyes. Something musty and woodsy has touched into my soul. [Your Ereb has a Malady; this item is corrupted.]

Data:Meringue.apple.json.Label: Baked Apple Meringue
Data:Meringue.apple.json.Desc: Harvey Hattington, during his convalescence at the House, was so obsessed with meringuing techniques that he was ultimately banned from the kitchen.

Data:Meringue.json.Label: Meringue
Data:Meringue.json.Desc: Add to milk for a legendary dessert. Or, with Spicing, add to, apples or pears - even to mushrooms, if you're feeling perverse.

Data:Meringue.mushroom.json.Label: Mushroom Meringue
Data:Meringue.mushroom.json.Desc: What in the Wolf-Divided's most splintered Name hath here been wrought?

Data:Meringue.pear.json.Label: Baked Pear Meringue
Data:Meringue.pear.json.Desc: Harvey Hattington, during his convalescence at the House, became obsessed with meringuing techniques. He was known to sneak down to the kitchens and interfere with the cooks in pursuit of his ideal.

Data:Meringue.ys.json.Label: Walls-of-Ys
Data:Meringue.ys.json.Desc: A frankly insensitive name that commemorates the inundation of that fabled city.

xexts.scrutiny: Doors can open to more than sight...

Data:Message.numa.invocation.json.label: Petition for a Labyrinth Season
Data:Message.numa.invocation.json.desc: If this ever reaches its destination, it might bring Numa.

xexts.posting: Numa cannot be bidden; but now and then, it has been successfully petitioned.

Data:Metal.json.label: Metal
Data:Metal.json.desc: This is what happens when stone gets serious.

Data:Mfet.json.label: Fet: Gisting
Data:Mfet.json.desc: In dreams I have visited the House behind the world... and some part of me is trapped there now, even when I wake.

xexts.malady．inflicting: As my concentration fails, a part of my soul flutters away, drawn by a distant half-imaginary light. [Your Fet has a Malady.]
xexts.contamination．winkwell: There are eyes here, half-visible, winking coyly at me. A winkwell infection. I keep thinking of those eyes when I close my own. [Your Fet has a Malady; this item is corrupted.]
xexts.contamination．curse．fifth．eye: This is cursed! The signs are unmistakable - a Fifth Eye curse which has wrenched open the unwilling eye of my soul. [Your Fet has a Malady; this item is cursed.]

Data:Midnight.mark.json.Label: Midnight Mark
Data:Midnight.mark.json.Desc: A blemish left on a page (or a skin) by a careful incision (or a judicious sting) to preserve a little of the power of night.

xexts.scrutiny: A little loss of night. [Certain Prentice-level Moon recipes can be used to make the Mark.]

Data:Milk.aspect.json.label: Milk
Data:Milk.aspect.json.comments: (Not visible - an aspect named milk that goes on the (probably cow's) milk element and possibly other milk elements if there are some)

Data:Milk.json.Label: Bottle of Milk
Data:Milk.json.Desc: [Mix in a bowl with Flour to make Dough - or pour over Meringue for a sweet dish celebrated at Claridge's.]

xexts.scrutiny: Your face in this glass looks scarred - older - harsher. A certain Door in dreams - it is said - opens only for a mirror which has just been cracked. But this mirror was cracked long ago.

Data:Mirror.frost.json.Label: Frosty Mirror
Data:Mirror.frost.json.Desc: A moon-coloured metal oval. It's shaped like a mirror, but no reflection is visible.

xexts.scrutiny: The frame has been carved with a quote from Blake - William, not Thirza: 'Prisons are built with stones of Law, Brothels with bricks of Religion.'
The glass returns reflected light with some reluctance, so even in broad daylight the effect is that of dusk.
Faint rust-specks dot the mirror. Or, just possibly, blood.

Data:Mirror.silver.json.Label: Silvery Mirror
Data:Mirror.silver.json.Desc: There are silvered mirrors, and there are silvery mirrors.

xexts.scrutiny: 'When the moon rises, the stars watch.'

Data:Mirror.storm.json.Label: Storm-Tossed Mirror
Data:Mirror.storm.json.Desc: Solid workmanship, but not obviously remarkable.

xexts.scrutiny: A plaque explains that in 1872 this mirror survived a shipwreck untouched, and was gifted to the House by a grateful survivor who was nursed back to health in the infirmary below.
Faint dents on the obverse suggest someone has taken out their impatience on this thing.

Data:Mission.autarchy.json.label: The Institute's Mission: Autarchy
Data:Mission.autarchy.json.desc: The Institute will learn to survive without the patronage of any Hour... so that one day, mortalkind can do the same.

Data:Mission.better.gods.json.label: The Institute's Mission: Better Gods
Data:Mission.better.gods.json.desc: The Institute will strive to create alternatives to the Hours - substitutes to the cosmic primalities that will be more benevolent, or more biddable.

Data:Mission.corrivality.json.label: The Institute's Mission: Corrivality
Data:Mission.corrivality.json.desc: The Corrivality sustains the world, literally and also metaphorically. Without the constant innovations and remaking of war, all humanity will stagnate. The Institute will ensure that does not happen.

Data:Mission.peace.json.label: The Institute's Mission: Peace
Data:Mission.peace.json.desc: In all the long-marked histories of thinkingkind, war has been an unimaginable scourge. The Institute will set itself to protecting the world from that scourge.

Data:Mission.revelation.json.label: The Institute's Mission: Revelation
Data:Mission.revelation.json.desc: Knowledge can be dangerous: but ignorance is more dangerous still. The Institute will work to free all mortalkind from the tyranny of Calyptra.

Data:Mission.secrecy.json.label: The Institute's Mission: Secrecy
Data:Mission.secrecy.json.desc: Some knowledge is too dangerous for the common mind. Calyptra might be tyrannous, but there is a truth at its core - and even if Calyptra were to fall, the Institute would take up their burden.

Data:Mission.stone.consumed.json.label: The Institute's Mission: Stone Consumed
Data:Mission.stone.consumed.json.desc: The gods-from-Stone came before the Hours we now know. Their return would be earthquake, famine, wilderness prowling the streets. It will not be permitted. But they are resources as precious as oil or gold or the knowledge in the marrow. The Institute will study them; uncover them; repurpose them, for the benefit of all mortalkind.

Data:Mission.stone.remembered.json.label: The Institute's Mission: Stone Remembered
Data:Mission.stone.remembered.json.desc: The gods-from-Stone came before the Hours we now know. Their return would be earthquake, famine, wilderness prowling the streets. It will not be permitted. But the Institute will study them; honour them; learn from their fall, to protect against another such change.

Data:Mission.uncertain.json.label: The Institute's Mission: Uncertain
Data:Mission.uncertain.json.desc: The Institute never resolved on a mission, beyond 'to keep all mortalkind from the rocks of eternal night.'

Data:Moly.aujus.json.Label: Moly au Jus
Data:Moly.aujus.json.Desc: This has been called 'Moth, but delicious, but perhaps we all will be, at the end.'

Data:Moly.json.Label: Moly
Data:Moly.json.Desc: 'Moly the gods call it, and it is hard for mortal men to dig; but with the gods all things are possible.' - Homer

Data:Moon.json.label: Moon
Data:Moon.json.desc: Secrets are soft; night is softer still; the sea speaks. It is not always wise to listen. [The nocturnal, the forgotten.]
